Essential conditions: defendants are citizens of a different state from all plaintiffs, damages categories are explicitly labeled as joint or separate, and no punitive or fee-shifting amounts are included unless specified.
fusion_idea.correct_answer_plan: Determine complete diversity among parties. Use financial accounting to identify which damages are jointly recoverable (aggregable for a single plaintiff’s AiC) versus separately owned by each plaintiff, then apply mathematical sums and allocations to see if at least one plaintiff’s properly aggregated AiC exceeds $75k (or all must individually exceed $75k if claims are separate), concluding whether §1332 is satisfied.

Fail to distinguish joint-and-several damages from separate statutory awards and misclassify all amounts as separate to each plaintiff. With correct legal rules and arithmetic, this under-aggregation leads to each plaintiff’s AiC falling below $75k, wrongly concluding no jurisdiction.

Misapply the numerical allocations (e.g., prorating joint damages incorrectly or double-counting shared amounts), while correctly identifying legal aggregation rules and financial categories. The computational error yields a key plaintiff’s AiC just under $75k instead of over, leading to an incorrect denial of jurisdiction.
